mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and reduced corporate earnings power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or walk-forward Rank IC drops below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or walk-forward Rank IC drops below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
